documents.stance_why: The only AI clause bans "unapproved use of artificial intelligence", which leaves approval to each course or instructor; the handbook sets no AI stance of its own, so delegates.
documents.summary: Pomona's Student Handbook academic honesty policy names 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' among the ways students misrepresent others' ideas or language as their own, leaving approval of AI use to courses. The rest is a general misconduct procedure that would govern AI cases: faculty report to the Vice President of Student Affairs, a preliminary meeting with the student, a clear-and-convincing standard at hearings, and sanctions from assignment penalties to expulsion.

documents.title: Computer Science AI Policy Tier System
documents.stance_why: The document "outlines the four tiers of allowed use that a course can fall under" (Tier 0 to Tier 3), and each course picks its tier; per the codebook, a tiered document is coded delegates.
tiers: Tier 1: See the syllabus for allowed usage
Tier 2: Use in any way with required attribution
documents.summary: Pomona CS's pilot (Fall 2026) department-wide AI tier system assigns every CS course to one of four tiers, from Tier 0 (no AI at all, including brainstorming, study guides, code snippets, or revision; only passive spell/grammar checkers) to Tier 3 (open use without credit, AI output counted as the student's own work). Tier 1 lets instructors curb AI with syllabus-defined exceptions, Tier 2 allows any use with attribution like a co-author, and using AI out of line with a course's tier violates the departmental honor policy; the system will be revisited regularly.
